flows.explanation: Questions on this flow no longer carry a single id: the reader can point at several things at once, as typed refs. `docair-ai.ask.ask` now builds what the question points at through the new `docair-ai.ask_context` module, which turns parts, lines, data and terms into words for the model and reports refs that name nothing; `docair-ai.client.chat` changed with it. On the server, `docair-server.ask_about` reads the refs from `docair-server.ask-context`, so "Ask about this" on a datum's page puts the datum into the question as a chip and the model gets the facts of everything picked.

flows.explanation: Two versions of a project can now be compared end to end: `docair-core.diff.diff` and `docair-core.changes.changes` diff the graphs and their flows, `docair-server.commits.graph_at` and `docair-server.commits.compare` scan each commit (cached, else from a scratch worktree), `docair-server.project.explain` serves `POST /api/explain`, and `docair-viewer.doc_page.render_page_with` with `docair-viewer.page_changes.change_view` and `docair-viewer.svg.draw_marked` show each changed flow's slice at A and B side by side. Asking gained context: `docair-server.ask` now goes through the new `docair-server.ask_about` and `docair-ai.ask_context.about`, which turns refs into words for the model via `docair-ai.ask_context.picture_at` and `docair-ai.ask_context.edge_words`, with `docair-core.ids.find` resolving what an id names for CLI, server and page alike. A tidy feature was added (`docair-core.tidy.repeated`, `docair-cli.tidy.cmd_tidy`, `docair-server.project.tidy_list`, `docair-viewer.page_tidy.tidy`) that lists hand-written tags the code repeats and offers them as a patch, and `docair-cli.cmd_check` and `docair-cli.cmd_scan` end with `docair-cli.tidy.hint`'s line while tags repeat. Plumbing moved too: `docair-server.upload_router` is gone with `docair-server.router` serving those routes itself, `docair-server.project.answered` was dropped, `docair-server.scan_root` picks the folder an upload is scanned from, and `docair-core.scan` now carries the fingerprints, edits, repeated tags and page pieces its outputs need.

The TypeScript linker was split into `docair-lang-ts.link_with_index` and `docair-lang-ts.link_inner`, so code references get certain call links from a code index, and `docair-viewer.doc-page.show` can now open a panel page (`docair-viewer.assets.page.panel`) for what an address names. Hiding a section is now the reader's own, in-page with Undo (`ask-spec.i-don-t-care-about-it-hides-it-and-undo-shows-it-again`), not a docair.toml change.

The raw answer from `docair-ai.client.chat` is parsed by the new `docair-ai.explain.reply_json`, which tolerates a ```json fence. The endpoint itself (`ai-endpoint`) stays the far end that answers with a walkthrough in JSON.

Asking now carries what the question points at: `docair-server.ask` reads the typed refs (`docair-server.ask-context.refs`), turns them into words with `docair-ai.ask_context.about`, and asks through the new `docair-server.ask_about`; a ref that names nothing is said to be left out. On kept uploads the question is forwarded by `docair-server.peers.forward` to the pod that keeps the upload, found through `k8s.svc.docair-server-peers`. The new test `ask-spec.a-question-points-at-parts-data-terms-and-lines` covers refs to parts, data, terms and lines at once.

flows.explanation: The health probe itself is unchanged: `docair-server.router` still answers `GET /healthz` for the kubelet. What was added is that `docair-server.main` now also resolves `k8s.svc.docair-server-peers`, the headless name by which the server pods find each other — the foundation the new peer forwarding builds on.

A kept upload now serves a full route set of its own: `docair-server.kept_upload_post` handles ask, word, glossary and apply under `/api/projects/<id>/api/…` (through `docair-server.kept_upload_any` to `docair-server.kept_upload_answer`), with `docair-server.kept_upload_preflight` for preflight. When this pod does not keep the upload, `docair-server.peers.forward` sends the request to the pod that does, found via `k8s.svc.docair-server-peers`. So an uploaded page asks the server that keeps it from any pod, and the conversation stays — as `ask-spec.an-uploaded-page-asks-the-server-that-keeps-it` checks.

flows.explanation: New endpoint `POST /api/explain`: `docair-server.project.explain` diffs the served project against a commit (`docair-server.commits.compare`, or `docair-server.commits.compare_work` with the already-built working-tree graph, via `docair-server.commits.git`), sends the flows without stored findings to the model through `docair-ai.explain.explain`, and rewrites the page with the findings (`docair-server.project.served-project.rewrite`) under `docair-server.project.served-project.lock`. An upload kept as a project has no git history, so it answers 409. The flow also shows the whole Kubernetes path: the browser reaches `docair-server.router` through `host-port`, `kind-node`, `k8s.traefik`, `k8s.ingress.docair` and `k8s.svc.docair-server`.

An upload is now kept under a pod-aware id: `docair-server.scan_upload` calls the new `docair-server.project.kept-uploads.keep_as`, which starts the id with the pod's own mark from `docair-server.peers.peers.prefix` when more than one server pod runs. The plain `docair-server.project.kept-uploads.keep` remains for the single-pod case, and the e2e test `ask-spec.an-uploaded-page-asks-the-server-that-keeps-it` still walks the uploaded page end to end.
